chunks: Sama'ah ibn Mihran narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام that he said:

“Whoever performs ʿumrah in Shawwal while intending to perform ʿumrah and return to his homeland, there is no harm in that. But if he remains until hajj, then he is performing tamattuʿ, because the months of hajj are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qaʿdah, and Dhu al-Hijjah. So whoever performs ʿumrah in them and remains until hajj, then it is mutʿah. And whoever returns to his homeland and does not remain until hajj, then it is an ʿumrah. If he performs ʿumrah in the month of Ramadan or before it, then remains until hajj, he is not performing tamattuʿ; rather, he is a resident visitor who has separated the ʿumrah. If he wishes to perform tamattuʿ in the months of hajj through ʿumrah leading to hajj, then let him go out from it until he passes Dhat ʿIrq or passes ʿUsfan, then enter performing tamattuʿ by an ʿumrah leading to hajj. And if he wishes to perform hajj separately, then let him go out to al-Jiʿranah and recite the talbiyah from there.”

key_terms.أَشْهُرَ الْحَجِّ: The designated months of hajj in which the rulings of tamattuʿ apply.
key_terms.الْجِعْرَانَةِ: A place from which one may enter ihram for an ifrad hajj in the case described.
key_terms.ذَاتَ عِرْقٍ: A boundary point mentioned as a place beyond which one exits before re-entering for tamattuʿ.
key_terms.شَوَّالٍ: The first of the months of hajj, during which ʿumrah may count toward tamattuʿ if one remains until hajj.
key_terms.عُمْرَةٌ: A standalone minor pilgrimage not treated as tamattuʿ when one does not remain until hajj.
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٌ: One performing hajj al-tamattuʿ by combining ʿumrah with hajj in the prescribed manner.
key_terms.مُتْعَةٌ: Here, the rite of tamattuʿ, meaning ʿumrah connected to hajj in the hajj months.
key_terms.مُجَاوِرٌ: A resident visitor staying in the sanctuary, not counted here as a mutamattiʿ.

ai.seo_question: When does an ʿumrah count as tamattuʿ for hajj, and when is it treated as a separate ʿumrah?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the fiqh of ʿumrah and hajj tamattuʿ based on the timing of the ʿumrah and whether the pilgrim remains until hajj. It distinguishes between a standalone ʿumrah, tamattuʿ during the months of hajj, and the ruling of one who had performed ʿumrah before those months and stayed on until hajj.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2937 - Sama'ah ibn Mehran narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

"Whoever performs Umrah in Shawwal with the intention of returning to their homeland without staying until Hajj, there is no harm in doing so. However, if they stay until Hajj, they are considered Mutamatti‘ (one performing Tamattu‘), as the months of Hajj are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah. Whoever performs Umrah during these months and stays until Hajj, it is Tamattu‘. But if they return to their homeland and do not stay until Hajj, it is considered merely an Umrah.
If one performs Umrah in Month of Ramadan or before it and stays until Hajj, they are not Mutamatti‘ but rather a Mujawir (resident performing separate Umrah and Hajj). In this case, the Umrah is considered separate. If they wish to perform Tamattu‘ in the months of Hajj, they must exit the state of Ihram by traveling beyond Dhat ‘Irq or Asfan and then re-enter in Ihram for Umrah, intending Tamattu‘ leading to Hajj.
If one prefers to perform only Hajj without Tamattu‘, they should go to al-Ji’ranah and enter Ihram from there."
